_: Where every animation comes from. Each sheet is one GPT generation, 1536x1024,
cut into a 4x4 grid of 384x256 cells; a cell downscales by 8 to a 48x32 grid of
art pixels, taking the mode of each 8x8 block and never the average — an average
makes mid greys, and a mid grey in a one-bit sprite is a soft edge.
The sheets here are not what came back from the generator. That was RGBA with a
fifth of every image in soft alpha, 5.9MB for eleven files, and the pipeline
reads none of it: only `alpha > 128`. They are stored as LA with a one-bit mask
in the alpha channel instead — same generated output, byte for byte, 121KB. The
soft edges are gone for good, so 8 and 128 are now baked in: a different block
size or a different threshold would have to start from new sheets.
cells are 1-based and inclusive; drop lists cells to leave out. blink names
cells holding the same frames with the eyes shut, in the same order — the face
is drawn into the art, so a blink has to be drawn too. There is no
alignment switch: every animation gets one offset putting its feet on the shared
ground line, which leaves whatever happens inside it — a gallop's float, a
leap — exactly as drawn. Scripts/make-sprites.py explains why.
That script turns this into Sources/AwayBlur/Render/CatFrames.swift.
